paper_summary: Japanese-language 1994 study (Seikei-Kakou 6(12) 877-882) of low density polyethylene syntactic foams filled with three hollow-particle systems: shirasu balloons (SB, 150 um, bulk sp. gr. 0.25, shell 1.3 um), polyester-coated shirasu balloons (SB-PEs) and glass microballoons (GMB, 80 um, bulk sp. gr. 0.20, shell estimated 1.11 um), at 5-20 vol% in 5% steps, compression moulded at 150 C into 1 mm sheets. Tensile tests at 0, 23 and 50 C showed Young's modulus increases with hollow-particle loading and rises roughly linearly with log strain rate, while the yield stress falls because the particles crush and void near yield; the reinforcing order is PE-SB+PEs > PE-SB > PE-GMB, attributed to shell thickness and surface roughness rather than particle size. Data were fitted with a Bruggeman modulus model (parameter x, Table 3) and a modified Nicolais-Narkis yield relation sigma_c/sigma_m = 1 - B*Vf^(2/3) (Table 4), where B is 1/2-1/3 of the solid-particle value 1.21.

processing.matrix_name: Low density polyethylene (Mitsubishi Yuka Yukalon PK-30), 'PE'
processing.particle_grade: Shirasu balloon, Ijichi Kasei Winlite SB-9011 (bulk sp. gr. 0.25 g/cm3, mean diameter 150 um)

structure.microstructure_notes: Shirasu (volcanic glass) balloon; shell thickness 1.3 um determined by two independent methods (crush/volume-ratio calculation 1.27 um and optical microscopy 1.33 um); cavity volume fraction of the particle (a/r0)^3 = 0.95. Rough, uneven particle surface. Blended by powder mixing and hot pressed into 1 mm thick sheets at 150 C, 10 min, then water quenched; the authors previously confirmed no particle fracture occurs in this pressure range. Filling 20 vol% of hollow particles gives about 15% weight saving.

test.specimen_notes: Toyo Baldwin Tensilon UTM-4LH / 5T with thermostatic chamber; JIS No. 2 dumbbell, 40 mm gauge (parallel) length, 1 mm thick sheet. Crosshead speed 5 mm/min (the condition of Figs. 1, 3 and 5); 5 mm/min over the 40 mm gauge length corresponds to about 2.08e-3 1/s. The same samples were also tested at 0 and 50 C, at crosshead speeds of 0.5, 50 and 500 mm/min, and (PE-SB and PE-SB+PEs only) at high speed 0.7752 m/s and 2.508 m/s at 23 C; those results appear only in figures, with no tabulated values.

evidence.quote: 複合材料の基材として,低密度ポリエチレン(三菱油化製YukaionPK-30,以後PEと略記する),中空微粒子としてシラスバルーン(イヂチ化成製ウインライトSB-9011,嵩比重0.259/cm3,平均粒径150μm,以後SBと略記する),およびガラスマイクロバルーン(東ソー製IG102,嵩比重0.209/cm3,平均粒径80μm,以後GMBと略記する)を使用した
上記,3種類の中空微粒子と基材PEとは,体積分率,y1=・5～20%の間,5%毎にパウダーミキシング法でブレンドし,ゴンノ油圧機製ホットプレスを使用し,温度150℃,最大加圧圧力30kgf/cm2
evidence.location: Sec. 2.1 (Preparation of samples), p. 878 - volume fractions Vf = 5-20% in 5% steps, hot press at 150 C

evidence.quote: の成形条件で,10分間加圧成形し,成形後水中に急冷して,厚さ1mmのシートを作製した.
低速引張試験は,東洋ボールドウィン製テンシロンUTM-4LHおよび5T型に恒温槽を付設して行った.測定温度は0。C,230Cおよび50。Cの恒温下で,引張速度は,0.5,5,50,500mm/min,試料形状は,・層JIS2号ダンベル形に切り出したものを使用した.
SBの殻厚を1.3μmとして,粒子の全体積に対する空洞の体積率y!α=〈α/猶o)3を求めると,0.95になる.

extraction_notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is a genuine hollow-particle (syntactic foam) paper, but the OCR'd text contains only the CAPTIONS of Tables 1-4 and Figs. 1-5, not their contents. Every quantitative mechanical result (Young's modulus, yield stress, composite density, the fitted Bruggeman x values and the fitted B parameters) exists only inside those tables and figures, so no property value could be read and all property fields are null. Per the extraction rules no values were estimated off the plots. 12 records are given, one per (filler system x volume fraction) actually fabricated: SB, SB+PEs and GMB at 5, 10, 15 and 20 vol%. Test conditions are recorded for the 23 C / 5 mm/min case used in Figs. 1, 3 and 5; the other conditions (0 C, 50 C; 0.5, 50, 500 mm/min; high-speed 0.7752 and 2.508 m/s) were not duplicated as separate records because they carry no readable values - they are listed in test.specimen_notes. Unfilled PE was also tested as the baseline but is not a hollow-particle composite, so it has no record. Derivations: strain_rate_per_s = 5 mm/min over the stated 40 mm JIS No. 2 gauge length = 2.08e-3 1/s. particle_wall_thickness_ratio (eta = inner/outer radius) is derived from stated numbers, not read directly: for SB the paper states shell 1.3 um on a 75 um mean radius and cavity volume ratio (a/r0)^3 = 0.95, both giving eta = 0.983; for GMB the estimated 1.11 um shell on a 40 um radius gives eta = 0.972. particle_true_density_g_cc is left null because 0.25 and 0.20 g/cm3 are BULK (tapped) specific gravities of the powders, not particle true densities. Composite densities (Table 2) are not in the text; only the statement that 20 vol% filling gives about 15% weight reduction. Shirasu balloons are hollow volcanic aluminosilicate glass; they are typed as ceramic_hollow to keep them distinct from the separately tested glass_microballoon (Tosoh IG102). LDPE has no dedicated matrix_class enum value, so other_thermoplastic is used. The paper's own '30 kgf/cm2 (29.4 MPa)' moulding pressure is internally inconsistent (30 kgf/cm2 = 2.94 MPa) and is not part of the schema, so it was not recorded.
